title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 29-31). L is a one-dimensional ordered 'line' with an adjoined boundary set ∂L, or ∂U. Tr(L) is the set of pseudo-slices ('pseudo-tranches') of L: points and interval-like pieces, ordered by T ≪ T' ('T lies strictly to the left of T' and is not adjacent to it'). A finite ≪-chain Φ = {T_1 ≪ … ≪ T_n} defines X_Φ = ⊔ T_i. Page 29 says the map Φ ↦ X_Φ is injective. Such sets are the 'parties modérées' (tame subsets, also called 'modulaires'). Their components are the T_i, so π_0(X) = {T_i}. The relative frontier is Fr(X) = (⋃∂T_i) minus ∂U, minus the endpoints that are not genuine boundary points.

Page 30. A point x ∈ L is 'in tame (transverse) position' with respect to X if it is so with respect to each component T_i, i.e. with respect to ⋃∂T_i outside ∂U, i.e. with respect to Fr(X). Examples: x ∈ X, or x outside Fr(X), has this property.

The tame complement is defined as X' = C_mod(X) = {x ∈ L∖X | x in tame position with respect to X}. Claim: X' is tame, and it is the largest tame Y ⊂ L∖X that is in tame relative position with X. Explicitly, if X is given by the diagram T_1 ≪ … ≪ T_n, then X' is given by:
- the n−1 interstitial slices between (T_1,T_2), …, (T_{n−1},T_n);
- plus, when they exist, the interstitial slice to the left of T_1 and the one to the right of T_n.

Marginal note: two tame sets X, Y are 'in tame relative position' if X ⊂ Y, or Y ⊂ X, or their frontiers are in suitable position, presumably Fr(X) ∩ Fr(Y) = ∅ or something similar; the end of the note is illegible.

Page 31 draws the consequences:
- The number n' of components of X' lies in {n−1, n, n+1}, so |#π_0(X) − #π_0(X')| ≤ 1, with the case split by whether the extreme slices are bounded on the outside.
- The poset Mod(L) carries three structures: inclusion, the 'modular pair' relation, and the subset of 'frank' tame sets.
- A left-margin note on p. 31 asks whether the modular relation is determined by the order (e.g. 'iff X ∩ Y exists').

This is the one-dimensional base case of a combinatorial 'tame topology via cuttings (découpages)'. It establishes that tame sets are closed under a tame complement, and it controls the count of connected components under that complement.
errors: The previous-page transcription writes both U_Φ and X_Φ for the same object; this is notational drift in the manuscript.
The tame-complement definition presumably should read C_mod(X) = {x ∈ L∖X | x in tame position w.r.t. X}. The transcription's 'C_mod(U)' and 'p.r. à U' look like misreadings, or a slip.
The maximality statement is only asserted ('Alors …'), not proved. It is evident from the explicit diagram description, provided adjacent slices are excluded by ≪.

On the next page the case analysis should concern T_1 and T_n, not T_1 and T_2. The labels 'non majoré/minoré' are also used loosely: the end slices exist exactly when T_1 has a lower bound or T_n an upper bound.

ideas.what: Tame subsets of a 1-dimensional ordered space as finite disjoint unions of non-adjacent slices (points/intervals), uniquely encoded by the slice diagram
ideas.modern_name: Definable sets in an o-minimal line / finite unions of points and intervals; cell decomposition in dimension 1
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is only programmatically sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); this combinatorial development appears unpublished

ideas.what: Tame complement C_mod(X) built from the interstitial slices, characterized as the largest tame set disjoint from X in tame relative position with it
ideas.modern_name: Complement of a definable set / pseudo-complement in the lattice of tame sets

ideas.what: Bound |#π_0(X) − #π_0(X')| ≤ 1, with precise case split by end behaviour
ideas.modern_name: Elementary component count for complements in 1D (Euler-characteristic-type bookkeeping)

ideas.what: Relation 'tame relative position' between tame subsets (nested, or frontiers in general position), studied as extra structure on the poset Mod(L)
ideas.modern_name: Transversality / general position of stratified sets; compatible pairs in a lattice

missed.claim: In 1986, independently and in purely order-combinatorial language, Grothendieck is axiomatizing the 1-dimensional base of tame topology. He uses slices, frontiers, tame complements and a 'tame position' relation, in parallel with the o-minimality formalism appearing in the same years. The added structure (a 'tame relative position' relation on the poset of tame sets) has no standard o-minimal counterpart.
missed.quote: Plus généralement, soit X, Y modérées, on dit X, Y en position rel. modérée si X ⊂ Y, ou Y ⊂ X, ou … Fr(X) ∩ Fr(Y)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest: it documents Grothendieck's own concrete attempt at the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse. The mathematics on this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the elementary 1-dimensional case of tame topology: complements of finite unions of intervals and a component count. It is historically interesting as Grothendieck's own development of the Esquisse's tame-topology programme, but there is no new mathematical result.
transcription_corrections: 'X' = C_mod(U) = {x ∈ L∖U | … p.r. à U}' should likely read C_mod(X), L∖X, 'p.r. à X'.
'x ∈ ∂U, de fonction de Fr(X)' likely reads 'x ∉ ∂U, en dehors de Fr(X)' (a point outside the frontier).
'telle que Y ∈ L∖X' should be 'Y ⊂ L∖X' (the crossed symbol is a crossed-out X replaced by Y).
'Alors [?]' contains a struck-out symbol (perhaps Ξ), not a word.
'parties modulaires' / 'modulaires' on the next page likely refers to the same 'modérées' sets.
Next page 'T_2 non majoré' should be 'T_n'.
